headline: Apple unveils new Apple TV 4K with Siri AI integration
summary: Apple's latest streaming box boasts a new A15 Bionic chip and a redesigned Siri remote with built-in microphones for voice commands.
details: Apple has announced a new Apple TV 4K, powered by the A15 Bionic chip for improved performance. This update brings enhanced graphics and faster processing to the streaming experience.

A key feature of the new Apple TV 4K is the redesigned Siri remote, which now includes built-in microphones. This allows users to interact with Siri directly from the remote for voice commands and searches.
The new Apple TV 4K also supports HDR10+ for improved color and contrast, alongside existing Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos support. This aims to deliver a more immersive viewing experience.

Alongside the Apple TV 4K, Apple also announced the HomePod mini 2, though it will not feature Siri AI integration at launch. Additionally, new Home Collection products like a video doorbell and smart lock were revealed.

headline_marked: Nvidia [[doubles DLSS 5 performance]] and cuts VRAM usage
headline: Nvidia doubles DLSS 5 performance and cuts VRAM usage
summary: The AI rendering tech for gaming is now twice as fast and uses 20% less VRAM, debuting in NBA 2K27.
details: Nvidia has announced significant upgrades to its DLSS 5 AI rendering technology for gaming. The latest model is now twice as fast as the previous version, representing a 10x performance leap since March, and it also reduces VRAM usage at 4K by up to 20%.

These improvements were achieved through optimizations in the rendering pipeline and refinements to the neural model. Nvidia claims that the GPU overhead has been halved compared to the September model, potentially boosting frame rates by up to 1.4x at similar visual fidelity.

The enhanced DLSS 5 model will first appear in NBA 2K27 on October 16, with Hogwarts Legacy also set to receive the update next month. Support continues for RTX 50-series GPUs, GeForce NOW, and the new RTX Spark lineup.

Additionally, Nvidia is rolling out a faster Performance Mode for Frame Generation on RTX 50 and 40 series GPUs, and RTX Spark laptops. A new algorithm replaces the previous one for calculating optical flow, offering a speed boost of up to 35% on the RTX 5060.
